name: Screw terminal block, 2-way, 5 mm pitch (KF301-2P, sold as 5.0 or 5.08 mm)
blurb: The blue two-way PCB screw terminal: an outside wire is clamped under each screw, so it can be taken off again with a screwdriver. Blocks slide together side by side for longer rows.

pins.note: Left clamp with the wire openings facing you. The outside wire is not soldered: strip 5 mm, push it into the opening under this screw and tighten. On a carrier PCB the leg under this screw is soldered to the board; in a hand-wired build the inside wire goes under the same screw (a twin ferrule holds two wires).
Right clamp with the wire openings facing you.

verify: Outline and legs are from a reseller's copy of the KF301 drawing, not from the maker (Cixi Kefa) directly: 10 x 7.5 mm, 10 mm tall, legs 5.00 mm apart, 2.5 mm in from each end and 3.5 mm from the back face, 4.5 mm long, 1.0 mm thick (1.4 mm holes). Blocks sold as 5.08 mm fit the same holes at 2 and 3 ways; the green KF128 and Phoenix MKDS types are deeper and taller, so measure depth and height of yours before a case depends on them. Wire openings are on the front face (y = 7.5); their size and height are drawn for recognition, not from the drawing. The 'wire entry' port is the whole front face of the block (from the outline), so a case wall the block stands against is opened over the full face; the real openings are in the lower part of it. Each pad is drawn on top of the block at its screw, above the leg. Rating on the sheet: 16 A, wire AWG 24 to 16, strip 4.5 to 5 mm, M2.5 screw, 0.4 Nm. Each pin is marked "screw": true, so the guide words an outside wire's end as clamped under the screw, not soldered.
